text:
maria (platform): Heads up — drafting a control-plane policy for Private (VPC / on-prem) customers. Goals: prevent egress to disallowed regions, ensure model-variant fallback never crosses allowed-region boundaries, and surface routing decisions + telemetry in Console. Looking for enforcement vs advisory takes.

raj (sre): strong +1 on enforcement for regulated customers. advisory ok for dev tiers. Question: are we allowing fallback to a compatible variant in another allowed region if the primary pool is full?

anya (product): Console UX should show a tiny 'routing decision path' in request details: matched policy -> chosen pool/zone -> variant -> fallback steps + reasons. A small timeline is enough.

derek (security): We can't allow automatic cross-region fallback for private customers who disallow egress. Policy must be explicit. Default: fallback_allowed = false for Private. If customers opt in, require an auditable justification and admin toggle.

julien (eng-runtime): On the runtime side we can restrict Router to variants where host_region ∈ allowed_regions. For on-prem folks with local model cache: we can prefer local artifacts, then dedicated pools in same region. Cross-region fallbacks require explicit permission.

maria (platform): Drafting a sample policy. Example YAML:
```yaml
control_plane_policy: 
  allowed_regions: [us-east-1, us-west-2]   # customer-owned allowed regions
  egress_mode: deny_with_logs            # deny outbound egress unless explicitly allowed
  fallback_policy: local_only            # options: local_only | allow_with_admin_approval
  telemetry: 
    emit_routing_decision: true
    sampling_rate: 1.0                   # always for enterprise customers
  blacklist_countries: [CN, RU]          # deny-by-country at control plane
```

raj (sre): telemetry fields we need: event_name=private.routing.decision, tags: customer_id, allowed_regions, selected_region, chosen_variant, fallback_reason, cost_delta, latency_est. Also include request tokens and routing path hash for traceability.

maria (platform): Proposed event example (for schema team):
```json
{
  "event": "private.routing.decision",
  "customer_id": "cust_1234",
  "allowed_regions": ["us-east-1"],
  "selected_region": "us-east-1",
  "chosen_variant": "gpt-4o-quant-8b-v1",
  "fallback_reason": "pool_capacity_exhausted",
  "cost_delta": 0.0023,
  "latency_est_ms": 120
}
```

policy-bot: RFC created -> RFC-234: "Private routing + fallback guardrails" (link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/234) :white_check_mark:

anya (product): UX idea: add a "simulate route" button in Console that takes a sample prompt + model preference and runs the same routing logic, showing the exact variant/pool it would pick and any policy blockers/warnings. Helps sales and SRE reproduce issues.

derek (security): Also require a policy validator that rejects policies which list allowed_regions that overlap with known restricted zones or blacklisted ASNs. Reject at policy creation time with clear feedback.

julien (eng-runtime): Implementation note: router pipeline will be two-pass: 1) filter candidate variants by allowed_regions + policy flags + quantization/arch constraints, 2) score by latency/cost/capacity. If after pass 1 the candidate set is empty -> return 409 + structured body: {"error":"no_compatible_variant","reasons":[...]} instead of attempting remote fallback.

raj (sre): We should also map this to quotas / reserved capacity. If fallback would route to a higher-cost pool that consumes committed capacity, we need to check commit usage and either deny or surface a billing hold.

maria (platform): Agreed. Decision: default enforcement mode = strict for private/enterprise. Add opt-in for "relaxed fallback" that requires admin consent and is audit-logged. Also add policy-linting in the Console before save.

deploy-bot: queued jobs: policy-validator (rfcs/234), routing-sim (preprod), telemetry-schema-check.

raj (sre): test plan: add unit tests for region-filter, integration test to simulate pool exhaustion, and a 48h canary on preprod with synthetic traffic and telemetry checks.

anya (product): I'll add the Console mockups to RFC-234 and include the simulate-route flow.

maria (platform): Please drop short comments on RFC-234 by EOD Fri. We want to get an initial canary staged next week. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/234

julien (eng-runtime): I'll prototype the router filter in a branch and add feature flags.

derek (security): I'll add the policy validation rules and a small compliance test matrix.

maria (platform): thanks all — leaving this thread open for quick async follow-ups. :thumbsup:

anya (product): :+1:

policy-bot: policy template added to /internal/policy-templates/private-routing.yaml

deploy-bot: CI: policy-validator passed for RFC-234 on branch feature/private-routing (build 4821).
